title: Regime manager: wire the client tracker/remapper into the session + close out TASK-25
description: TASK-25.1 lands the full green suite. This task finishes TASK-25: (a) makes acceptance criteria 3–4 real in the running client — RegimeTracker (src/client/state/regime.ts) and ControlsRemapper (src/client/input/controls.ts) exist and are unit-tested, but nothing instantiates them; wire them into the client session so the client tracks its own regime live (planets from the known system, server authority from its own entity_update flightRegime, local prediction from the last known flight state, controls remap + debug log on change); (b) does the TASK-25 bookkeeping and the final feat commit. Scope guard: there is NO live keyboard→flight-input path and no local-prediction frame loop yet (src/client/net/prediction.ts is not wired live; the rendered world is still the placeholder from TASK-8; surface streaming is TASK-26, camera TASK-27, atmosphere visuals TASK-28, disembark TASK-31) — build the regime plumbing those tasks will consume, do not build flight input, prediction, or rendering.

steps.description: Make the surface sub-state server-authoritative in the client tracker
steps.details: The client has no terrain yet: systemRegimePlanets (src/shared/galaxy/planets.ts) leaves heightAt unset → flat ground at 0, while the server injects the chunk-cached TerrainContext heightAt. So a local surface prediction over real relief would disagree with the server around every landing and the 500 ms snap+warning would fire repeatedly. Extend src/client/state/regime.ts (client-only module — do NOT touch src/shared/regime.ts): ANY local↔server disagreement that involves 'surface' is expected, not a bug — the active regime follows the server immediately, with NO divergence clock and NO warning; the 500 ms divergence clock + snap + debug warning remain for space/atmosphere disagreements (identical same-seed anchor data must agree there — beyond the tolerance it is a bug, per the spec). Keep every existing test in src/client/state/regime.test.ts green and add unit tests: server 'surface' with local 'atmosphere' (flat terrain, ship low and slow) → active follows the server with no divergence warning and no snap; server 'atmosphere' with local 'surface' → same, follows server, no warning; a genuine space/atmosphere divergence still snaps to the server at 500 ms with the warning. Verify: cd app && npx vitest run src/client/state/regime.test.ts

steps.description: Wiring module + session integration in main.tsx
steps.details: Create a small client module (suggested: src/client/state/regime-wiring.ts; keep files ~300 lines max per repo standards — main.tsx is already 537 lines, so add only a few lines there) that owns one RegimeTracker + one ControlsRemapper with: setSystem(seed, systemId) → tracker.reset() + tracker.setPlanets(systemRegimePlanets(systemForId(seed, systemId).planets)); onSelfUpdate(entityState, nowMs) → if entityState.flightRegime is present, tracker.applyServer(entityState.flightRegime, …), then tracker.updateLocal(entityState.pos, vecLength(entityState.vel), nowMs) — the last known flight state at 10 Hz is the client's prediction stand-in until TASK-26 provides a per-frame local sim; tracker onRegimeChange → remapper.setRegime (which logs the swap — debug). In useGameSession (src/client/main.tsx): route inbound entity_update messages whose payload.callsign === session.callsign into the wiring — ClientSession.onMessage (src/client/net/session.ts, ~line 423) already delivers ALL inbound messages; the handler there currently ignores everything but 'chat' and 'presence'; call setSystem when systemId is known (systemForId(serverSeed, systemId) is the existing pattern, main.tsx ~line 322) and reset on system change/reconnect. Add a unit test for the wiring module with a synthetic message stream: first self entity_update with flightRegime 'atmosphere' → active control scheme switches space→atmosphere (remapper.setRegime called, no divergence warning); further self updates keep it; a system change (setSystem) resets to space. Verify: cd app && npx vitest run src/client, npm run typecheck, npm run lint.

cd app && npm run test → full unit suite green (0 failures). npm run typecheck + npm run lint clean. Optional smoke only if time remains (the wiring now runs in the live client): one existing e2e spec (npm run test:e2e -- core-flow) boots the game with no NEW console errors — the regime remap has no visible UI yet (its consumers are TASK-27/31), so e2e beyond that boot smoke is not required; note in the commit/log if skipped.

.ralph/tasks.json — mark this task (TASK-25.2) passes: true with all steps pass: true. .ralph/logs/LOG.md — entry, newest on top, summarizing TASK-25 completion (stale atmosphere fixtures fixed in TASK-25.1, client tracker/remapper wiring + surface server-authority rule in TASK-25.2, suite green). .ralph/STRUCTURE.md — add the module list (no test files): src/shared/regime.ts, src/shared/galaxy/planets.ts, src/client/input/controls.ts, src/client/state/regime.ts, plus the new wiring module. Delete .ralph/handoff/TASK-25.md in the final commit. Final commit (Conventional): 'feat(TASK-25): regime manager — seamless space/atmosphere/surface transitions'.

acceptanceCriteria: The running client tracks its own regime: tracker + remapper instantiated from the session, planets from systemRegimePlanets(systemForId(seed, systemId).planets), server authority from self entity_update flightRegime (payload.callsign === session.callsign), controls remap with debug log on regime change, reset on system change

src/client/state/regime.ts: any local↔server disagreement involving 'surface' does not start the divergence clock (no snap, no warning around landings on flat terrain) — the active regime follows the server; a space/atmosphere disagreement still snaps to the server after 500 ms with a debug warning, and the existing divergence test still passes

Wiring unit test with a synthetic self entity_update stream: flightRegime 'atmosphere' flips the active control scheme space→atmosphere without a divergence warning, and a system change resets to space
cd app && npm run test: full unit suite green (0 failures); npm run typecheck + npm run lint clean
TASK-25 closed out: .ralph/tasks.json passes, .ralph/logs/LOG.md entry, .ralph/STRUCTURE.md updated, .ralph/handoff/TASK-25.md deleted, final feat(TASK-25) commit landed
notes: Builds on TASK-25.1 (HEAD has the full green suite). Wiring facts (verified in the code): ClientSession.onMessage (src/client/net/session.ts, ~line 423) delivers ALL inbound messages; useGameSession in src/client/main.tsx currently handles only 'chat' and 'presence'. entity_update payload = EntityState (src/shared/protocol/schemas.ts, entityStateSchema): {id, kind, pos, vel, rot?, regime, flightRegime?, hull, shields, targetId, classId, callsign?, livery?} — NOTE: 'regime' is the wire enum sublight|cruise|warp|docked and is NOT the flight regime; the regime manager's value is the optional 'flightRegime' (FLIGHT_REGIMES = space|atmosphere|surface), sent by the server on every entity_update (src/server/shard/shard.ts, ~line 861); treat a missing flightRegime (v1 back-compat, optional on the wire) as 'no authority update' (keep the current server value). Planet data: systemRegimePlanets maps orbital-slot order to anchors (planetAnchor(i) = ((i+1) × 10000, 0)); heightAt stays unset client-side (flat 0) until TASK-26 gives the client terrain — that is why the surface sub-state is server-authoritative (step 1). RegimeTracker API (src/client/state/regime.ts): setPlanets / reset / updateLocal(pos, speed, nowMs) / applyServer(regime, planetId) / regime / planetId / divergenceMs(nowMs); REGIME_DIVERGENCE_MS = 500. ControlsRemapper API (src/client/input/controls.ts): CONTROL_SCHEMES per regime (space flight, atmosphere flight + VTOL key, surface walk/look/interact stub — TASK-31 fills the behavior) + remapper.setRegime with a debug log. Do NOT build: keyboard→flight input, a local-prediction frame loop, rendering changes, or e2e coverage of the remap itself (consumers are TASK-26/27/28/31). Do NOT touch src/shared/regime.ts or the server. Conventions: prettier (npm run lint includes prettier --check), Conventional Commits, one task per invocation — commit and stop.
